fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Epic 62dc's criterion 5 is undelivered: plan review never tells a reviewer that the plan under review overlaps work another ticket already describes. Each plan is read in isolation, so two tickets planning one change both pass, the duplication surfacing later or not at all.

Create-time surfacing matches a title plus a short description. Plan review runs later against a full plan -- far more material -- as the last gate before work starts. One index serves both.

## Approach

**Reuse the index; add no second retrieval path.** The sibling story builds a lexical FTS5 index under `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/`, caught up in the read phase with no daemon. Its whole public surface is `find_similar` (`src/rebar/similar/__init__.py:46-54`, stated at `:8`). It **already** takes arbitrary query text via `text=` (`:51`, resolved at `:73`) plus `exclude_id=` to drop self-hits (`:52`), so querying it with plan material needs no new retrieval module. With the optional embedding tier configured it ranks through that tier, otherwise lexically (`:79-82`), inheriting the sibling's portability: it works with no model provider configured.

**The one gap: failure distinguishability.** `find_similar` collapses every failure to an empty list -- absent index `[]` (`:63-64`), catch-up failure warns then `[]` (`:67-72`), any other exception warns then `[]` (`:83-85`), the "Never raises" property at `:55`. A caller cannot tell an absent index from a failed catch-up from an empty match.

**Diagnostic contract.** `find_similar` gains one keyword-only parameter `diagnostics: dict | None = None`. When a dict is passed, it records a `status` from the closed set `ok`, `index-absent`, `catch-up-failed`, `provider-error`, plus a human `detail`. Return type, "Never raises", every existing call stay unchanged: the signal travels through the caller-supplied dict rather than the return value. The only `src/` consumer is the create path at `src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:196` (imported `:27`), which passes no `diagnostics`.

**Recording channel: the existing coverage merge.** The status is recorded under `coverage["overlap"]` via the `coverage_extra` seam, which `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py:132` accepts then `:153` merges into `coverage`, documented at `:140` as carrying "e.g. a diagnostic record" -- the mechanism `:120` uses for `not_claimable`. Tests assert `coverage["overlap"]["status"]`, a defined field, not a log line.

**Ride the existing Pass-1 extra-context seam.** A Pass-1 finder unit already accepts store-derived `extra_context` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:54`), its identity binding that context by `context_digest`, a sha256 over the injected text (`:61-63`, carried at `:70`), under the Pass-1 discovery contract `plan_review_findings` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:122`). That text is built by `_chunk_extra_context` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:215`), whose single call site `:326` feeds `_discovery_unit_plan` `:331` plus `checkpoint_identity` `:339`; `checkpoints.py` never builds the value, so `pass1.py` is where injection lands. The seam is live today: `:219-222` already injects G5 decomposition context. Appending candidates there rather than adding a pass keeps checkpoint identity plus caching unchanged -- a changed candidate set yields a different `context_digest`, correctly invalidating the checkpoint.

**Zero marginal LLM cost: the existing Pass-1 unit does the judging.** Candidates ride a chunk already being sent, so overlap judging adds no LLM call whatever its outcome; lexical retrieval is not an LLM call either. The cap that matters is therefore on injected candidates rather than calls, asserted by a test because an unasserted cap silently grows.

**On demand, not on every review.** The switch is one keyword-only parameter `overlap: bool = False` on `review_plan` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:199`), threaded to `run_pass1` (`pass1.py:232`) then `_chunk_extra_context`. Default off: a review not passing `overlap=True` injects nothing, its checkpoint identity unchanged.

**Findings are advisory.** An overlap finding names the candidate ticket plus why it overlaps; it never BLOCKs. A child, a follow-up, a deliberate split each overlap by construction, so blocking would stall correct decompositions.

**Degradation.** On any non-`ok` status the candidate list is empty, no overlap finding is emitted, the review proceeding to its normal verdict. Retrieval cannot change an outcome by failing.

**The injection site has little headroom, so the work is extracted rather than appended.** `pass1.py` is 658 lines against the 800 cap in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`. Overlap retrieval plus its diagnostic therefore live in a new `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/overlap.py`; `_chunk_extra_context` gains only the call.

Any ratcheted mechanism this adds carries a `# mechanism-ok:` marker naming this ticket at its definition site; `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` fails otherwise.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `overlap=True`, reviewing a ticket whose plan restates an existing ticket's plan emits an advisory overlap finding naming that ticket. Checked by: a seeded-store test asserting the finding names that ticket id.
- [ ] Retrieval offers more than 10 candidates on a store seeded with more than 10 matches. `RESULT_LIMIT` is 5 (`src/rebar/similar/lexical.py:39`), so retrieval must raise `limit` above its default or the cap below is vacuously true. Checked by: a test asserting the retrieval result length exceeds 10.
- [ ] At most 10 candidates are injected into the Pass-1 extra context. Checked by: a test on a store seeded with more than 10 matches asserting exactly 10 were injected.
- [ ] With `overlap=True`, the number of LLM calls equals the number made by the same review with `overlap=False`. Checked by: a test comparing both call counts.
- [ ] With `overlap=False`, no overlap finding is emitted. Checked by: a test asserting the finding set is empty.
- [ ] With `overlap=False`, the run's checkpoint identity is byte-identical to the same review before this change. Checked by: a test comparing the computed identity against the unmodified path.
- [ ] An overlap finding never changes a review's verdict from pass to block. Checked by: a test asserting a passing plan's verdict is unchanged with an overlap finding present.
- [ ] `find_similar` called without `diagnostics` returns exactly what it returned before this change. Checked by: a test asserting the `recent_creates.py:196` call yields an unchanged result.
- [ ] With no model provider configured, overlap retrieval still returns lexical-tier candidates. Checked by: a test with provider credentials cleared asserting a non-empty injected candidate set.
- [ ] When the index is absent, the verdict equals that of the same review with `overlap=False`. Checked by: a test comparing both verdicts.
- [ ] When the index is absent, `coverage["overlap"]["status"]` is `index-absent`. Checked by: a test asserting that value, with the overlap finding set empty.
- [ ] When catch-up raises, the verdict equals that of the same review with `overlap=False`. Checked by: a test comparing both verdicts.
- [ ] When catch-up raises, `coverage["overlap"]["status"]` is `catch-up-failed`. Checked by: a test asserting that value, with the overlap finding set empty.
- [ ] When the embedding provider errors, the verdict equals that of the same review with `overlap=False`. Checked by: a test comparing both verdicts.
- [ ] When the embedding provider errors, `coverage["overlap"]["status"]` is `provider-error`. Checked by: a test asserting that value, with the overlap finding set empty.
- [ ] Every module added or modified under `src/rebar/` is at most 800 lines. Checked by: the module-size gate.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0. Checked by: running it.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0. Checked by: running it.
